_comment: Verifier verdict vectors for chain format v4, continued chains and v7 anchors. Written by scripts/verdict-vectors.py from docs/format-spec.md (§2.0, §2.5, §5.0, §9.3, §9.7) and never by an implementation under test. chain_cases: as in verify_verdict_vectors.json, and expected.erased_found counts v4 erased entries. bind_cases: a keyless bind of a v7 anchor to entries (linked from previous_hash when given) with the caller's expect (subject, previous_anchor_hash; empty means not given); expected.error true means the anchor or the bind is refused; otherwise compare outcome, bound, tombstones, entries_not_bound and subject_checked. expected.breaks in chain_cases is how many breaks a walk reports, every one collected. entries_text_cases: text (or, for bytes that are not UTF-8, text_base64) is an entries file; "entries" if it reads, "not_entries" if the reader refuses it (an error, never a broken chain). No case needs a key.

chain_cases.name: intact
chain_cases.why: §2.0: four live v4 entries

chain_cases.name: erased_entry
chain_cases.why: §5.0: an erased entry is recomputed from its leaf hash; not a break

chain_cases.name: entries_before_an_erased_entry_rewritten
chain_cases.why: §5.0: the attack v3 cannot detect. The erased entry is recomputed from the forged predecessor, so it no longer matches

chain_cases.name: entries_before_an_erased_entry_rewritten_and_everything_relinked
chain_cases.why: §5.0: with the whole chain relinked it is consistent again, and the head changed: only an anchor catches it (see bind case rewritten_and_relinked)

chain_cases.name: entry_id_changed
chain_cases.why: §2.0: the id is in the leaf hash

chain_cases.name: entry_type_changed
chain_cases.why: §2.0: the type is in the leaf hash

chain_cases.name: stored_leaf_hash_wrong
chain_cases.why: §5.0: a live entry's leaf hash is recomputed and compared

chain_cases.name: erased_leaf_hash_replaced
chain_cases.why: §5.0: the chain hash is recomputed from the leaf hash

chain_cases.name: erased_without_the_right_to
chain_cases.why: verification-model, Who may erase: THE PROPERTY. An erasure is not authenticated by the chain; this chain verifies whoever erased the entry

chain_cases.name: salt_missing
chain_cases.why: §2.0: a live entry carries its salt

chain_cases.name: erased_with_entry_id_kept
chain_cases.why: §2.0: an erased entry carries no id

chain_cases.name: erased_false
chain_cases.why: §2.0: a live entry carries no erased member

chain_cases.name: tombstone_type
chain_cases.why: §2.0: v4 has no tombstones

chain_cases.name: tombstone_type_and_id
chain_cases.why: §2.0: the v3 tombstone shape, in a v4 entry

chain_cases.name: run_id_member
chain_cases.why: §2.0: absent, not empty

chain_cases.name: first_entry_not_at_zero
chain_cases.why: §2.0: a v4 entry with no predecessor has global_seq 0

chain_cases.name: continued_from_v3
chain_cases.why: §2.5: a v3 chain from global_seq 1, continued in v4

chain_cases.name: continued_after_a_v3_tombstone
chain_cases.why: §2.5: the v3 prefix keeps exactly its guarantee

chain_cases.name: continued_v3_prefix_rewritten_before_its_tombstone
chain_cases.why: §2.5, §5.5: the v3 limitation stays in the prefix, and is reported; the v4 entries add nothing to it

chain_cases.name: v3_entry_after_v4
chain_cases.why: §2.5: never back from v4

chain_cases.name: v3_tombstone_after_v4
chain_cases.why: §2.5: the load-bearing case. A v3 tombstone's chain hash would be taken as stored and unlink everything before it

chain_cases.name: erased_entries_after_a_break_are_counted
chain_cases.why: §5.5: every entry walked is counted, after the first break too

chain_cases.name: erased_entry_with_a_malformed_chain_hash_is_not_counted
chain_cases.why: §5.5: an entry is counted only once its chain_hash is in shape (step 2)

chain_cases.name: v3_tombstone_after_a_v4_entry_broken_at_step_2
chain_cases.why: §2.5, §5.5: never back from v4 goes by the declared format, even after a v4 entry that broke at step 2, so the v3 tombstone after it is refused at step 3 and not counted

chain_cases.name: misuse_before_timestamp
chain_cases.why: §5.5: step 3 before step 5

chain_cases.name: timestamp_before_shape
chain_cases.why: §5.5: step 5 before step 7

chain_cases.name: sequence_gap_first
chain_cases.why: §5.5: step 1

chain_cases.name: segment_with_its_predecessor_hash
chain_cases.why: §2.0: a segment links from the hash supplied

chain_cases.name: segment_without_its_predecessor_hash
chain_cases.why: §2.0: the first entry's global_seq is above 0, so it has a predecessor and this is a segment; walked from nothing, it breaks the first-entry rule

chain_cases.name: predecessor_hash_supplied_to_a_first_entry
chain_cases.why: §2.0: an entry with a predecessor has global_seq above 0

chain_cases.name: leaf_and_chain_hash_both_wrong
chain_cases.why: §5.0: a leaf mismatch is the entry's one break, and its stored chain_hash is not compared; the walk goes on from the hash the recomputed leaf gives, so entry 2 links

chain_cases.name: timestamp_in_another_spelling
chain_cases.why: §4, §5.5: the same instant spelled otherwise is invalid_timestamp, and the walk goes on from the stored chain hash: one break, not a mismatch here and after

chain_cases.name: timestamp_in_another_spelling_and_chain_hash_wrong
chain_cases.why: §5.5: step 5 ends the entry's checks; the next entries are judged from its stored (wrong) chain hash

chain_cases.name: erased_entry_with_a_bad_timestamp
chain_cases.why: §5.5: an erased entry's timestamp is checked like any other

chain_cases.name: erased_entry_with_a_tombstone_type
chain_cases.why: §5.5: step 3 (a tombstone shape) comes before step 7 (an erased entry carries no type)

chain_cases.name: v4_then_v3_then_v4
chain_cases.why: §2.5: never back from v4; the v4 entry after it is judged on its own

chain_cases.name: live_leaf_hash_uppercase
chain_cases.why: §5.5: a shape break (step 7), before the leaf is compared

chain_cases.name: continued_v3_entry_after_its_tombstone_rewritten
chain_cases.why: §2.5: v3 binds the entries after its last tombstone, and the first v4 entry links from the v3 head, so rewriting a v3 entry after the tombstone and relinking the v3 part breaks at the first v4 entry

chain_cases.name: v3_tombstone_with_two_defects
chain_cases.why: §5.5 step 4: a tombstone's checks in order, the first its one break: the content hash before the run fields

chain_cases.name: malformed_supplied_previous_hash
chain_cases.why: §5.5 step 7: the first entry's break; the next links from its stored hash

chain_cases.name: nel_and_nbsp_in_entry_id
chain_cases.why: §2.0: U+0085 and U+00A0 are not control characters there

entries_text_cases.name: surrogate_pair_escape
entries_text_cases.why: §2.0: a pair is one character, read as it

entries_text_cases.name: salt_in_another_spelling
entries_text_cases.why: §5.5: one spelling and one JSON type per member, null for none

entries_text_cases.why: §5.5: one spelling and one JSON type per member, null for none

entries_text_cases.why: §5.5: one spelling and one JSON type per member, null for none

bind_cases.name: first_entry_erased
bind_cases.why: §5.0, §9.4: erasure changes nothing the anchor binds; a v6 anchor broke here

bind_cases.name: last_entry_erased
bind_cases.why: §5.0, §9.4: erasure changes nothing the anchor binds; a v6 anchor broke here

bind_cases.name: first_and_last_erased
bind_cases.why: §5.0, §9.4: erasure changes nothing the anchor binds; a v6 anchor broke here

bind_cases.name: rewritten_and_relinked
bind_cases.why: §5.0: before an erased entry, rewritten and the whole chain relinked; it verifies alone, and the anchor's head no longer matches

bind_cases.name: other_subject_expected
bind_cases.why: §9.7: a genuine anchor for another subject

bind_cases.name: subject_checked_before_the_head
bind_cases.why: §9.7: two defects, a wrong head and another expected subject; the subject is step 5, the head step 6

bind_cases.name: predecessor_checked_before_the_subject
bind_cases.why: §9.7: two defects, another expected predecessor and another expected subject; step 4 is reported

bind_cases.name: chain_broken
bind_cases.why: §9.7 step 1: the chain is walked first; a break is chain_broken whatever else differs

bind_cases.name: no_subject_expected
bind_cases.why: §9.7: bound, and the result says the subject was not checked

bind_cases.name: other_predecessor_expected
bind_cases.why: §9.7: the caller expected another previous anchor

bind_cases.name: later_anchor_naming_the_seed_id
bind_cases.why: §9.3: the seed id goes with the seed hash only

bind_cases.name: chain_grown_since_the_anchor
bind_cases.why: §9.7: the tip is the entry at end_seq; entries after it are not the anchor's business

bind_cases.name: truncated_from_the_front_and_relinked
bind_cases.why: §9.7: renumbered from 0 it is a whole chain again, one entry short; the tip it names is not the one signed

bind_cases.name: over_a_segment
bind_cases.why: §9.8: an anchor is not bound to entries verified from a predecessor hash

bind_cases.name: continued_chain_from_seq_1
bind_cases.why: §2.5, §9.7: start_seq is the chain's first global_seq

bind_cases.name: range_not_from_the_first_entry
bind_cases.why: §9.7: start_seq names the chain's first entry

bind_cases.name: continued_after_a_v3_tombstone
bind_cases.why: §2.5: the v3 prefix up to its last tombstone is reported unbound

bind_cases.name: continued_v3_prefix_rewritten_before_its_tombstone
bind_cases.why: §2.5: the frozen v3 limitation, against a v7 anchor. It binds, and entries_not_bound is what tells the caller
